name: Adrianne Lenker
label: 4AD
lede: A Minnesota kid who wrote her first song at eight, made four Big Thief records in four years, and went into the woods with a tape machine for her best solo album.

eras.title: A cult, a railroad spike, a karate belt
eras.text: Adrianne Lenker was born in Indianapolis and raised mostly in Minnesota after her family left the religious group it had joined. By thirteen she was recording an album with her father as manager.

years.h: Born in Indianapolis, into a cult she leaves before age five
years.p: Wikipedia says Lenker's family left the Christian group it belonged to when she was about four, then moved through a run of rented homes, fourteen of them by the time she was eight.
years.xp:
At five, a railroad spike fell from a treehouse roof in Nisswa, Minnesota, and lodged in her skull. She survived, and later described it in the Big Thief song "Mythological Beauty".

She was homeschooled, wrote her first song at eight and, per Wikipedia, took up karate hard enough to win the Minnesota state title three years running.

eras.title: Fourteen, then Berklee
eras.text: A teenage record, a GED at sixteen and a Boston scholarship set up the move to Brooklyn, where a chance meeting in a grocery store shaped the next decade.

years.h: Stages of the Sun: a debut at age fourteen
years.p: Lenker's first album came out on the small LucidTunes label, the same year as a live record, Live at the Southern.

years.h: Berklee on Susan Tedeschi's scholarship, where she meets Buck Meek
years.p: After a GED at sixteen, Lenker went to Berklee College of Music in Boston on a scholarship funded by [[Susan Tedeschi|deabe097-2a03-49ce-9ae3-c9645bc778c7]] and met the guitarist [[Buck Meek|b8780175-4ff4-4d87-8e54-999f70dbb5ec]] at a concert.
years.xp: When Lenker moved to Brooklyn she ran into Meek again at Mr. Kiwi, a Bushwick grocery store, on the day she arrived. The two started playing together, and Meek became a constant in her music.

eras.title: Bushwick, tape and a duo
eras.text: Self-released records and a co-written LP with Meek came before anyone called it a band.

years.h: Hours Were the Birds, self-released first
years.p: Lenker's second solo album came out on her own; a-sides and b-sides, with Buck Meek, followed on May 1. Saddle Creek reissued both on November 16, 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Masterpiece (Big Thief album) · Wikipedia: Adrianne Lenker
years.h: Big Thief tracks Masterpiece on Lake Champlain
years.p: The quartet of Lenker, Buck Meek, bassist Max Oleartchik and drummer Jason Burger cut the debut in Essex, New York, with producer [[Andrew Sarlo|700b0a0c-9c3b-44b3-8de4-51c1a5f4b2e1]].
years.xp: Wikipedia credits [[James Krivchenia|611cb5a3-42cd-4aef-98e6-5749b88bf63a]] with engineering and additional production on the record. Krivchenia was first hired to engineer the debut and later replaced Burger on drums.

eras.title: Four records in four years
eras.text: Big Thief turned out an album a year while Lenker kept writing solo songs on the road, and the band moved from Saddle Creek to 4AD.

years.h: Masterpiece lands on Saddle Creek
years.p: Pitchfork's Jill Mapes gave Big Thief's debut 7.7; the cover is a childhood photograph of Lenker's mother with a toy dinosaur.

years.h: Capacity, written in a house-sat farmhouse
years.p: The band recorded for about a month in a farmhouse in upstate New York, with overdubs at Black Lodge in Brooklyn.

years.h: Abysskiss: ten songs, 33 minutes, two of them reborn
years.p: Recorded at Panoramic House in West Marin, California, with producer [[Luke Temple|27c978f2-284d-469f-a116-23f7fca9a6fc]]; "Terminal Paradise" and "From" returned with the full band on U.F.O.F.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Jayson Greene gave it 8 out of 10. The album, per Wikipedia, was built from songs written on tour with Big Thief.

years.h: Lenker and Buck Meek divorce and keep the band
years.p: Wikipedia says the two split in 2018 and stayed in Big Thief as close friends.

years.h: U.F.O.F. arrives on 4AD and gets a 9.2
years.p: Recorded in June 2018 at Bear Creek in Woodinville, Washington; Pitchfork named it Best New Music.

years.h: Two Hands follows five months later, Grammy-nominated for "Not"
years.p: Cut at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas, with nearly all the vocals live; Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland called "Not" a towering statement.

eras.title: Pine cabin, then a double album
eras.text: The pandemic cancelled a European tour and sent Lenker to a one-room cabin in Massachusetts, and the recordings became her first 4AD solo releases.

years.h: A pine cabin in Westhampton, an eight-track, and a paintbrush
years.p: Lenker and engineer [[Philip Weinrobe|3d5aa701-6cad-4bfe-8e42-fde78fc7123d]] recorded for a month, working on an Otari tape machine the duo got mid-session.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that the sessions opened and closed each day with improvised guitar pieces that became instrumentals. The palette included a paintbrush and white pine needles, with rain, wind, a wood stove and birds on tape.

The two albums came out together on October 23, 2020 via 4AD, and songs placed 11th on Pitchfork's 2020 list.

years.h: songs and instrumentals drop the same day on 4AD
years.p: Metacritic scored songs 84 from 19 reviews; "Anything" and "Dragon Eyes" led the way.

years.h: Tiny Desk (Home) Concert from a trailer in Joshua Tree
years.p: NPR's pandemic-era Tiny Desk series filmed Lenker in a camper in Joshua Tree National Park.

eras.title: A bright future, recorded twice over
eras.text: After a double album with the band, Lenker went back into the woods with Weinrobe and friends and cut the record Pitchfork ranked among the year's best.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
years.h: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You: 20 songs from 45
years.p: Big Thief tracked it in five locations from April to December 2020, and Pitchfork awarded it 9.0.
years.xp: The album earned two Grammy nominations, for Best Alternative Music Album and, for "Certainty", Best Alternative Music Performance.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album) · Stereogum: Premature Evaluation
years.h: Double Infinity studio: Nick Hakim, Mat Davidson and Josefin Runsteen join Lenker
years.p: The sessions for Bright Future ran in fall 2022 at a woodland studio in a 150-year-old New England building.
years.xp: Nobody stopped a take, and Lenker did not listen back until the other players had left, per Wikipedia. Weinrobe told the record's liner account: "Adrianne and I never once looked at a computer screen."

years.h: "Ruined" is the first single from Bright Future
years.p: The lead single came with an official video, and a live version with Nick Hakim followed from Greenwich Village.

years.h: I Won't Let Go of Your Hand goes up on Bandcamp
years.p: Lenker self-released the EP, with proceeds going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album) · Stereogum: Premature Evaluation
years.h: Bright Future on 4AD: piano, banjo, violin, no drums
years.p: Twelve songs in 43 minutes, recorded live to tape; "Real House" and "Free Treasure" (co-written with James Krivchenia) are the standouts in Stereogum's Premature Evaluation.
years.xp: The album was released on 4AD on March 22, 2024 and charted at No. 5 on the US Heat list and No. 18 on Folk, per Wikipedia. It earned Lenker her first solo Grammy nomination, for Best Folk Album.

q: It feels like I'm following an invisible thread of intuition.
years.src: Album of the Year: Adrianne Lenker, Bright Future · Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album)
years.h: Pitchfork gives Bright Future an 8.4 and ranks it No. 23 of the year
years.p: Andy Cush's review, scored 8.4 per Album of the Year, praised the record's space between spontaneity and craft.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the review as Best New Music, and Pitchfork ranked the album No. 23 on its list of the year's 50 best. Slant and The Vinyl Factory put it second in their year-end lists; Uncut placed it sixth.

years.h: Max Oleartchik leaves Big Thief
years.p: The band announced that the founding bassist was out "for interpersonal reasons" and with mutual respect.

eras.title: Back to the trio
eras.text: Lenker, Buck Meek and James Krivchenia made the first Big Thief album without Oleartchik and released a live solo tape from a Portland show.

years.h: Double Infinity: Big Thief as a trio
years.p: Produced by Dom Monks at Power Station in New York with ten session players including Laraaji; Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
